correctness.rationale: Every rank-one square-zero factor is uniquely represented by a normalized nonzero vector and annihilating functional. For nonzero C, equality AB=C forces unique line alignment, giving a bijection with alpha(u0)=beta0(x)=0 and alpha(x)=1. Restricted pairing is perfect when trace(C) is nonzero and has one-dimensional left/right radicals when trace(C)=0. The zero product is counted by image lines in ker(alpha). Exact counts and BA=trace(C) x alpha prove all cases. Direct finite-field arithmetic exhaustively verifies all targets for nine (n,q) settings.

originality.rationale: The inspected full primary papers address existence of nilpotent factorizations or commuting nilpotent similarity classes. Their statements and proofs do not determine the exact product-fiber cardinalities or the reversed-product dichotomy for two minimal-nilpotent factors. Six actual semantic queries against the published research index, supplemented by broader literature searches, found related but not equivalent claims. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: An exact product convolution of the canonical minimal nonzero nilpotent conjugacy class is a natural invariant linked to established nilpotent-factorization problems, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The law gives all target fibers over every finite field and dimension, a sharp n=2 exceptional boundary, and the nontrivial reversed-product zero criterion. Previously known existence criteria do not determine these multiplicities.
